Adobe stock: Here are 5 strategic questions into new leadership
Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs maintained its "sell" rating on Adobe as Anil Chakravarthy prepares to take over as president and CEO on Dec. 1, saying competition is intensifying and new entrants are gaining ground in areas that could expand Adobe's market.
Before you buy NVIDIA: our AI model's stock picks are beating the market by 120%+. See the list now »
The broker said it wants clearer evidence of Adobe's strategy and execution before changing its view. It sees the leadership change as a potential catalyst, but said the market remains concerned that artificial intelligence could weigh on Adobe's growth.
Chakravarthy's appointment follows a transition announced in March. He previously led Adobe's Customer Experience Orchestration business and worldwide field operations. David Wadhwani, who headed the Creativity & Productivity business, is also leaving to start a new venture, while Adobe is appointing a permanent chief financial officer.
Goldman said a successful turnaround will depend on Adobe simplifying its product architecture, speeding up innovation through internal investment and targeted acquisitions, and converting adoption of new features into revenue. The key question is whether the new management makes significant strategic changes or largely extends the existing three- to five-year plan.
Goldman highlighted five areas to watch:
Not finding the right stocks? Our AI's list of investor-grade stock picks for October just dropped »
Firefly: Adobe has shifted from relying mainly on its own Firefly models toward using Creative Cloud as a platform that brings together multiple third-party AI models.
Goldman said this moves Adobe's focus from competing on AI model quality to controlling the workflow. Firefly initially stood out because its models were trained on Adobe Stock, licensed content and public-domain material.
Acquisitions: Goldman expects Adobe to pursue smaller deals that add technology and engineering talent rather than make a large transformational acquisition.
It pointed to Salesforce and Workday as examples of companies taking a similar approach, although potential targets could command high valuations.
User growth: Monthly active users across Acrobat, Creative Cloud, Express and Firefly exceeded 1 billion in the third quarter, up more than 20% from a year earlier.
Adobe is seeking to turn that growth into revenue through free-to-paid conversions, higher-priced plans such as CC Pro and charges for users who exceed their included generative AI credits.
Express: Goldman said Adobe's uneven product development has left Express trailing Canva, which has more than 265 million monthly users and at least $4 billion in annual recurring revenue. Goldman estimated Express had about 70 million monthly users in 2025.
Customer experience: Adobe is repositioning Experience Cloud, which accounts for about a quarter of subscription revenue and is growing at a low-teens rate excluding Semrush, as a platform for managing AI-driven customer experiences.
Goldman said it remains unclear whether this orchestration role can become a valuable business in its own right or mainly serves to protect Adobe's existing software products.

pages.title: Adobe Still Has $24.5 Billion Left for Buybacks. That's About a Quarter of the Company. | The Motley Fool
pages.text:
▲ S&P 500 +---%|▲ Stock Advisor +---%Join The Motley Fool
Shares of Adobe (ADBE -1.49%) have had a tough 2026. The stock ended last year at about $350 and trades near $240 as I write, down about 31%.
The software company has kept buying its own shares on the way down. In April, its board approved a new $25 billion stock buyback authorization, meant partly to "reduce share count over time." It runs through April 30, 2030.
And as Adobe's fiscal third quarter of 2026 ended Aug. 28, $24.55 billion of it was still unused.
Compared with Adobe's market value, the amount is large. With about 389.2 million shares outstanding in mid-September, Adobe is worth about $93 billion at today's stock price. The remaining authorization could buy back about 26% of it -- about 102 million shares.
Sure, an authorization isn't a promise. Adobe has around three and a half years to use it, and nothing forces the company to spend it all. But I think the company's pace this year shows it plans to put plenty of it to work.
Image source: Getty Images.
In the fiscal year's first three quarters, Adobe's buybacks averaged around $2.3 billion a quarter. That came to $6.82 billion, for 26.1 million shares, all bought on the open market.
And as the stock dropped, the same money bought more shares. The 9.5 million shares Adobe repurchased in fiscal Q3 cost an average of around $235 each, versus about $261 over all three quarters.
Notably, the company paid for it with cash from its operations. Adobe generated $7.65 billion of cash from operations during the same stretch, up around 11% year over year, and buybacks used close to 90% of it. Its balance sheet had $5.64 billion of cash and short-term investments at quarter-end, versus around $6.4 billion of debt.
This pace leaves room to spare. Spreading the unspent $24.55 billion evenly through April 2030 comes out to around $7 billion a year, about what Adobe spent in just those three quarters. If the company keeps buying at its recent rate instead, it could use up the authorization sometime in 2029.
Adobe's diluted share count (the number used to calculate earnings per share) was around 395 million in the fiscal third quarter. That compares to 402 million in the fiscal second quarter and 424 million in the year-ago quarter.
Management's fourth-quarter targets assume around 389 million. In other words, the count's dropping about 2% a quarter, and steadily.
Not every repurchased share sticks, though. Shares outstanding dropped by around 22 million in the nine months, fewer than the 26.1 million Adobe bought, because employee stock awards added some back.
Showing what the shrinking count means for shareholders, Adobe's non-GAAP (adjusted) net income rose around 8% year over year in fiscal Q3 to $2.42 billion. Adjusted earnings per share climbed 15% to $6.13.
On a GAAP basis, net income grew just 3%, but earnings per share climbed 11% to $4.62. In short, fewer shares drove about half of the quarter's adjusted per-share growth.
If Adobe spent all $24.55 billion at roughly $240 a share and its earnings stayed flat, retiring about 26% of its shares would raise earnings per share by over a third.
That won't happen all at once, and the price Adobe pays will move. A lower stock price would stretch the cash further, and a higher one would shrink it.
$93BMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary.
Is the buyback a reason to buy?
At roughly $240, Adobe shares cost about 13 times earnings. Using the midpoint of management's fiscal 2026 target for adjusted earnings per share ($24.45 to $24.50), the price is about 10 times adjusted earnings. When shares reached their 52-week high of $363.70, that same target worked out to almost 15 times adjusted earnings.
I'd say buying back stock at about 10 times adjusted earnings is one of the better uses of Adobe's cash right now.
True, a buyback can't fix slowing growth. Adobe's total annualized recurring revenue (ARR), its gauge of the subscription business on a yearly basis, rose 11.2% year over year in fiscal Q3, and management's full-year target is 10.2%. And the market's discount probably reflects worries that artificial intelligence tools might hurt Adobe's pricing power. But as long as the subscription business keeps growing, a falling share count should help earnings per share outpace the business itself.
All in all, I think the buyback makes a cheap stock more interesting. Adobe stock looks worth considering at this price, but I'd want the subscription business to keep growing at roughly its current pace.

The Adobe Stock Debate Is About to Get Interesting
Adobe beat earnings for the fifth straight quarter, yet the stock sits 31% in the hole for the year while a generative AI rival just torched its retail sentiment. Something has to give, and the answer depends on a bet…
Published October 2, 2026, 1:30pm ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Adobe is a multinational software company best known for its Photoshop and Acrobat. © Adobe logo (CC by 2.0) by midiman
Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE | ADBE Price Prediction) trades at $239.94. Our 24/7 Wall St. price target is $286.62 over the next 12 months, which means 19.45% upside. Our model rates the stock a buy, and its confidence level is high.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
The debate: can Adobe convert surging AI engagement into durable revenue faster than generative AI rivals erode its creative moat? At 9x forward earnings, the market is pricing in a decline the financials have yet to show.
Adobe Slid 31% in 2026 Despite a Q3 Beat
The stock is down 31.31% year to date and 17.89% over the past month, and it was flat over the past week. That leaves it about 34% below its 52-week high of $363.70 and 26% off its $190.12 low.
Fiscal Q3 revenue of $6.76B beat the $6.70B consensus, and non-GAAP EPS of $6.13 topped expectations for a 5th consecutive quarter. Management raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $24.45 to $24.50.
Retail sentiment turned bearish after OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.5. Investors also face a leadership change: Anil Chakravarthy takes over as CEO on December 1st.
AI-first ARR topped $650 million, up more than 150% year over year. Monthly active users passed 1 billion, and Firefly ARR grew 40% quarter over quarter. Adobe also has $24.55 billion left on its buyback authorization.
Analysts expect fiscal 2027 EPS of $27.6733, and their consensus target is $275.06. In our bull scenario, the stock reaches $320.65.
Wall Street remains cautious, with 23 Hold ratings against 5 Sell or Strong Sell ratings. One analyst noted net new ARR fell “36, 37%” year over year, while remaining performance obligations grew only 8%.
Management prioritizes freemium user acquisition and delays pricing actions, which bulls see as investment in future conversion. Our bear case is at $249.08.
Adobe Trades at a Steep Discount to Salesforce and Autodesk
Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) competes directly with Adobe Experience Cloud for enterprise customer-experience budgets. The stock changes hands at 14x forward earnings, with quarterly revenue growth of 10.8%. Adobe is growing faster at a lower multiple.
Autodesk (NASDAQ:ADSK) is the closest subscription design-software peer. It commands 18x forward earnings, with revenue growth of 16.1%.
Our target means a forward multiple still below both peers. Against this group, the 24/7 Wall St. price target looks conservative.
The 24/7 Wall St. price target of $286.62 comes with a buy rating and 90% confidence. What tips the scale for me is Adobe’s single-digit forward multiple sitting alongside double-digit growth.
The setup looks compelling if freemium users start converting into ARR during the seasonally strong fourth quarter. Caution makes sense if net new ARR keeps shrinking under the new CEO. I think the market is too pessimistic here.
Looking further ahead, here is where our model projects Adobe could trade by the end of each year, assuming current growth trends and market conditions hold.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
Adobe would need to keep executing on its agentic AI strategy for these projections to hold. Faster Firefly monetization could add significant upside, while losing creative share to generative AI rivals is the biggest downside risk.

Her work has appeared on sites that include The Motley Fool, InvestorPlace, and Benzinga. She covers investing and focuses on stock picks and price prediction for 24/7 Wall St.

For College Students Who Want to Earn Money on CrowdWorks | Which Adobe Software Should You Actually Use? [Introductory Part 1]
Last time, in my job hunting experience report, I
thought about 'how much AI can be used in job hunting.' Thank you to everyone who read it!
Starting this time, as promised, I will be delivering three 'Introductory' articles in a row.
In this note, I have been mentioning the names of Adobe apps like 'Photoshop,' 'Premiere Pro,' and 'Firefly' as if everyone already knew them.
'What is the difference between Photoshop and Illustrator?'
most basic parts, have I...
So this time, I have organized the big picture of Adobe from scratch for those who 'hear the names but don't really understand them'🍓
what I confirmed on the official Adobe website as of October 4, 2026.
Adobe's prices and campaigns change often, so
please be sure to check the latest information on the official website before signing up.
Adobe is the 'company name,' Creative Cloud is the 'subscription name'
Let's start with the part that is most confusing.
Adobe: The name of an American software company
Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, etc.: The names of apps made by Adobe
Creative Cloud: The name of the subscription that allows you to use those apps for a monthly or annual fee
In other words, saying 'I'm using Adobe'
actually means 'I'm using one of Adobe's apps'
to be precise.
In the past, buying software outright was the mainstream, but
now it is basically a subscription (a form where you pay money every month or year to use it).
There are over 20 apps in Creative Cloud, but
these are the ones you often hear about for side hustles and content creation.
By the way, regarding the work I have written about in my previous articles,
Banner/Logo Creation → Photoshop (+Firefly) (Articles 5, 11-15, 18)
Video Editing → Premiere Pro (Article 8)
are the main ones.
※On the Adobe official website's pricing page, Premiere Pro has recently been listed as
"Adobe Premiere." In this note, I will continue to refer to it as
"Premiere Pro" as I have before.
What beginners find most confusing: The difference between Photoshop and Illustrator
These two look the same in that they are both "apps for creating images." The difference lies in
the way the images themselves are created.
Photoshop: Handles images as a collection of tiny colored dots (pixels). Great for photo editing and textured banners.
Illustrator: Draws shapes by calculating the positions of points and lines (vector). Since the lines don't get jagged no matter how much you zoom in, it's great for logos and printed materials.
To visualize it, Photoshop is like "painting with paints," while
Illustrator is like "drawing with a ruler and compass"🍓
In my fifth article, I wrote about how I made a logo using Photoshop x Firefly. However, for professional logo design projects,
clients may request delivery in Illustrator format (.ai, .svg, etc.) which doesn't degrade when scaled up or down, so if you want to focus on logo work,
I recommend keeping Illustrator in mind as well.
So, which one should I use?
This is the most important point I want to convey this time.
Instead of asking "which app is the best," I recommend working backward from "what kind of work do you want to do?".
I want to do banner/thumbnail work → Photoshop
I want to do logo/icon work → Illustrator
I want to do video editing work → Premiere
I want to try making SNS post images first → Adobe Express or Canva (can start for free)
If you try to learn everything at once, you'll probably get discouraged...
I wasn't able to use everything from the start either;
I added them little by little to match the work I wanted to take on.
How much does it cost? (As of October 4, 2026)
From here on, it's about money. I've summarized the main plans for individuals
that I checked on the official Adobe website (all prices include tax and are for monthly payments on an annual plan).
*For the standard version of Creative Cloud Pro, there was also a campaign offering a discount for the first 12 months for first-time subscribers (this varies depending on the time of year).
Honestly, it's expensive for college students, isn't it...
If you're a student, the 'student discount' is overwhelmingly the best deal
However, if you are a student or faculty member, the story changes.
According to the official Adobe website, Creative Cloud Pro for students and faculty is available on an
From the 4th month onwards: 2,180 yen/month
From the 2nd year onwards: 4,180 yen/month
(campaign price as of October 4, 2026).
the student discount for Creative Cloud Pro (2,180 yen from the 4th month) is cheaper than the Photoshop single-app plan (3,280 yen)
.
In other words, if you're a student, rather than choosing a single-app plan thinking 'I'll just start with Photoshop,' it's cheaper and you get more apps if you sign up with the student discount, right?🍓
Points to note about the student discount
I've also summarized the points I thought were worth being careful about while researching.
Verified via school email address: Your eligibility is verified when you enter a school-issued email address (such as .ac.jp) at the time of purchase. If it cannot be verified, it seems you may be asked for proof such as a student ID.
Annual plans assume a 1-year commitment: Even with monthly payments, it is a '1-year contract.' However, the official website states that if you cancel within 14 days of the start of billing, you will receive a full refund.
Price increases from the 2nd year: Once the first-year discount ends, the price will go up even if you remain on the student rate. You'll definitely want to check the renewal timing.
You can try it for free first: A 7-day free trial is also available for students. I recommend trying it out before signing up.
What's the difference from Canva?
When it comes to side hustles or content creation, Canva is always compared.
Broadly speaking, Canva's strengths are 'speed and ease,' while Adobe's are 'flexibility and professional applicability.'
It's not so much that one is better than the other; they just have different roles.
In fact, when looking at side-hustle job postings, there are
Adobe apps or file formats, such as 'Photoshop proficiency required' or 'deliver in PSD format.'
If you want to take on these kinds of jobs, being able to use Adobe is a prerequisite.
On the other hand, for social media posts or simple flyers,
Canva is often more than enough.
Therefore, I think it's perfectly fine to start by using Canva (free) to experience 'what it means to design,' and then move on to Adobe once you see the kind of work you want to do
A deeper realization: Choose your tools by working backward from the 'work you want to do'
This is what I felt most strongly after researching this time.
I tend to want to explain the app's features. But when thinking about it as a side hustle, what really matters is 'what kind of work can I get with that app?'
after all.
Want to take on banner design jobs → Photoshop
Project specifies PSD format → Photoshop
Want to deliver logos in a format that won't pixelate when scaled → Illustrator
By deciding which apps you need from the perspective of the work like this,
you won't get lost among the 20+ available apps.
This might be rooted in the same idea as what I wrote in the 17th post: 'To get repeat requests,
think about what the other party is looking for.'🍓
Adobe is the company name, and Creative Cloud is the name of the subscription that lets you use all the apps together
Decide which app to use by working backward from the 'work you want to do'
If you're a student, the Creative Cloud Pro student discount is cheaper and a better deal than a single-app plan (though be aware of the price increase from the second year)
If you're unsure, it's okay to start with Canva or Adobe Express (free) first
I hope this has softened your image of 'Adobe = difficult and expensive' even just a little bit🍓

'Photoshop x CrowdWorks: Are there jobs that beginners can take?'
.
I wrote in this post that 'you can take on banner jobs with Photoshop,' but I plan to summarize what kind of projects are actually on CrowdWorks, what beginners should learn first, the types of jobs that are difficult to do with just Canva, and include my own experiences with banner competitions and logo creation. I would be happy if you followed me and stayed tuned🍓

pages.title: Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant Review for Research Reading
pages.text:
AI in Education / Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant Review: Reading and Exploring Research Documents
When research involves long PDFs, finding a relevant passage can take considerable time. We might remember a finding without recalling its location, or need to compare how several papers address the same question. In this Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant review, I examine its summaries, document questions, source links, and uses for educators and researchers.
Its appeal is the connection between the response and the document. I would use that connection to locate evidence and guide reading, while checking whether the cited material supports the answer.
What Is Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant?
Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant provides conversational tools for working with documents in Acrobat. It lets users ask questions, generate summaries, and explore collections through PDF Spaces.
It fits research reading and document analysis. For a literature review, I would use it after collecting suitable sources, alongside a reference manager and my own reading notes.
Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant Review: Main Features
You can open a PDF, select AI Assistant, and type a question or choose a suggested one. Adobe’s documentation describes answers with source citations and follow-up suggestions.
For researchers, useful questions might include:
What research question does this paper address?
How did the authors select their participants?
Which limitations do they acknowledge?
Where do they explain this finding?
I would begin with a specific question tied to the document. Asking where the authors discuss a limitation is more manageable than requesting a judgement about whether the entire study is trustworthy.
Adobe’s AI Assistant instructions explain that selecting a source number takes you to the relevant section.
This is one of the features I would prioritize when evaluating a research-reading tool. It gives us a practical route for checking the response against the paper.
However, a citation does not establish that an answer is accurate. Read the surrounding passage, examine qualifications, and check whether the response has converted a tentative claim into a definite conclusion.
Also distinguish these document citations from bibliographic references. A link to a passage helps verify an answer; it does not automatically provide the reference entry required for a manuscript.
Acrobat’s Generative Summary produces an overview with section headings and summaries. Adobe also describes cross-references that let readers move from the summary to the corresponding source section.
I would use this to plan a reading session. After reviewing the overview, identify the sections most relevant to your question and examine them directly.
For empirical papers, check whether the summary preserves the relationship between the method and the conclusion. A finding makes more sense when we know who participated, what was measured, and what the design can establish.
PDF Spaces brings related files into a shared workspace where users can ask questions across the content. Adobe’s documentation lists support for organizing up to 100 files in a space, adding notes, saving useful responses, and sharing the workspace.
For research, I would begin with a small collection around a clearly defined question. Ask how the papers define a concept or how their methods differ, then check the relevant documents individually.
A larger collection can be convenient, but it also creates more opportunities to merge findings that should remain separate. Keep study populations, settings, and measures visible when comparing sources.
Related: Zotero Reference Management Review
Use audio overviews and share reading collections
Adobe also offers podcast-style document overviews and sharing options through PDF Spaces.
An audio overview could help someone revisit a collection before a meeting or identify sections to read later. It should be treated as another generated representation of the sources.
Sharing could support a research team or graduate reading group. I would agree on the collection’s purpose and permissions before inviting others. A shared workspace is most useful when contributors know which sources belong there and what notes they should add.
Questions about a PDFLocate methods, findings, or limitations
Source-linked responsesCheck an answer against its supporting passage
PDF SpacesExplore a selected document collection
Saved notes and responsesRecord questions for further examination
Audio overviewsRevisit material before reading or discussion
Workspace sharingCoordinate a reading collection
Prepare for detailed reading. Generate an overview, identify relevant sections, and read them yourself. Note where the overview omits information needed to interpret the findings.
Compare study methods. Ask about sampling, data collection, or outcome measures across a small set of papers. Verify each comparison before incorporating it into your literature review.
Recover evidence during writing. Use a question to locate the passage behind a note or claim. Check the original wording before quoting or paraphrasing it.
Prepare a research meeting. Gather selected papers in a PDF Space and save questions that need discussion. Keep unresolved issues visible.
These are suggested workflows, whose value depends on the documents, the questions, and the accuracy of the responses.
Teachers could use Acrobat AI Assistant to introduce source-checking activities. Students first read a short section, then examine an AI answer and its cited passage. Ask them whether the passage supports the answer and which qualifications need to be retained.
Another activity could compare a generated summary with the original abstract or conclusion. Students identify what each version emphasizes and what they need to read elsewhere in the paper.
For graduate seminars, a small PDF Space could support discussion of methodological differences. The task should require students to explain those differences using the original studies.
Full access is available through eligible Acrobat plans or an AI Assistant add-on. Adobe’s current offerings include plans such as Acrobat Express and Acrobat Studio, while institutional access may depend on licensing and administrator settings.
Check the official plans page for your country and account type. Pricing, included features, and billing commitments vary, so a displayed monthly figure should be read alongside its annual or monthly contract terms.
Before purchasing, confirm whether your institution already provides access. A standard Acrobat subscription should not be assumed to include every AI feature.
Adobe’s technical requirements, checked on October 1, 2026, list files below 100 MB and up to 600 pages. PDFs should not have password protection or usage restrictions. An internet connection and a supported Adobe account are required.
The requirements also state that AI Assistant does not support images or complex vector graphics. This matters when interpreting research figures: do not assume that an answer about a document includes a reliable analysis of its charts.
Language support varies by feature and platform. Check the current requirements when working with multilingual literature.
Adobe states that customer content is not used to train the generative AI models delivering Acrobat features. That statement still needs to be considered alongside institutional rules for confidential materials and document sharing. In PDF Spaces, inspect access permissions before distributing a collection.
Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant is worth considering if much of your research reading already happens in Acrobat. Questions, summaries, and PDF Spaces offer several ways to navigate documents while keeping sources accessible.
I would assess it using papers you already know. Check whether answers point to supporting passages, summaries preserve limitations, and comparisons keep studies distinct. Those checks provide a more useful basis for choosing the tool than the fluency of its responses.

pages.title: Adobe ChatGPT plugin gets interactive editing
pages.text:
Adobe puts brushes and sliders inside ChatGPT's image editing
Adobe's ChatGPT plugin now has interactive editors: brush a selection, tweak sliders for hue or contrast, and more
Adobe ChatGPT plugin gets interactive editing
Adobe's ChatGPT plugin gains interactive editors for images, designs, and PDFs. Users can brush a selection, tweak sliders, and edit PDF text from side panels in the ChatGPT window.
Following last week’s addition of tools into Google Gemini and expansion of Claude capabilities, Adobe has now added interactive editing experiences to the Adobe plugin in ChatGPT. Announced alongside OpenAI's DevDay 2026 unveils, the new capabilities cover images, designs, and PDFs, and appear in side panels in the ChatGPT chat window.
The image and design editors are powered by Photoshop and Adobe Express. Users can select part of an image in the interactive editor, ask ChatGPT to use the Adobe plugin to make changes, then fine-tune the result with new controls. They can pick out objects or brush over areas, then adjust hue, saturation, contrast, and more with sliders.
One useful UI feature is that the editor surfaces controls based on the type of edit; asking for an object's color to change brings up color controls scoped to that selection, and so on. Edits stay in context as users move between the editor and the conversation, without re-explaining the work or re-uploading the content.
Adobe’s Deepti Pradeep illustrates in a blog post how this all works. “Say you're capturing a lifestyle photo of a latte on a coffee table for a social post, and there's a stray napkin in the shot. Open the image in the side panel, select it with the brush tool, and request a focused change — ‘remove the napkin from the table.’ Once the napkin is removed, you can continue refining the same image. To make the latte pop more, focus on the cup again with the brush tool and ask ChatGPT to use the Adobe plugin to adjust its brightness and contrast. Adobe dynamically surfaces sliders for both, so you can fine-tune the image to get the look you're going for.”
PDFs, meanwhile, open in a side panel using Acrobat tools. Users can revise text or highlight passages in place, then send that document context back to ChatGPT to continue the task.
In one example that will hit home with plenty of people, a user highlights a paragraph about payment terms in a freelance contract and asks ChatGPT to use the Adobe plugin to highlight other sections about payments or invoicing.
Adobe recently unified its creative and productivity tools in a single plugin across ChatGPT, Claude, and Slack. These updates are already rolling out globally on ChatGPT web and app.

Adobe, NHL partner to deliver AI-powered fan experience
Technology will help deliver ability to personalize content, enable individual creativity
Adobe and the National Hockey League Partner to Deliver AI-Powered Fan Experiences Globally
As an Official Creative, Marketing and AI Partner of the National Hockey League (NHL), Adobe is providing AI technology to support the NHL’s global expansion efforts, delivering the ability to highly personalize fan experiences and enable individual creativity.
As the game moves beyond the arena and across digital channels, Adobe CX Enterprise solutions will activate AI for the NHL to deliver the right fan experience, at just the right moment.
In the future, the partnership could give fans AI-powered tools to express their love of the sport and its Players—content they can share on social platforms and beyond.
SAN JOSE and NEW YORK -- Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE) — the global technology leader that unleashes creativity, productivity and customer experiences through innovative tools and platforms — and the National Hockey League (NHL) have announced a partnership to transform fan experiences with AI. As the NHL gets ready to drop the puck on the 2026-27 regular season, Adobe becomes an Official Creative, Marketing and AI Partner of the NHL. Adobe will provide AI technology to help power how the NHL creates and personalizes fan experiences across every touchpoint, as the League looks to expand its footprint globally (with over 200 million fans across 147 countries) and deepen engagement with its audiences. The partnership could also provide fans new creativity tools to express their passion for the sport and its Players.
“The NHL's greatest strength has always been the passion our fans bring to the game,” said David Lehanski, NHL Executive Vice President of Innovation and Growth Strategy. “As the ways people follow sports continue to evolve, our focus is on creating experiences that feel as dynamic and compelling as the game itself. Adobe will help us unlock new ways to tell the stories of our Players, Clubs and moments that define hockey, while giving fans more opportunities to be a part of it. This partnership reflects our commitment in continuing to evolve how fans connect with the game they love.”
“The National Hockey League has built an extraordinary connection with its fans, and Adobe is helping them take that relationship to the next level by using AI to deepen personalization and empower everyone to create," said Lara Balazs, CMO and EVP of global marketing, Adobe. "With Adobe's enterprise solutions, the League will be able to scale relevant, engaging content across every channel where fans spend their time, fueling operational efficiencies and unlocking individual creativity."
The Adobe and NHL partnership will provide the League and its 32 Clubs access to Adobe CX Enterprise solutions, combining marketing, creativity and AI tools to drive impactful customer experiences. Over 20,000 brands across industries leverage Adobe solutions to drive Customer Experience Orchestration (CXO), creating systems where organizations can anticipate customer intent and ensure interactions are relevant and engaging. The NHL is partnering with Adobe to enhance fan experiences through accelerating CXO and drive its long-term growth strategy.
Adobe and the NHL will partner on AI initiatives including:
On-brand content, at global scale: Adobe GenStudio—the AI-powered content supply chain solution—will help the NHL transform how it creates and delivers content, keeping pace with the speed of the game and fan expectations. By powering the content production process with AI, the League can easily create highly personalized experiences for channels such as NHL.com, the NHL app, social media and digital advertising, while also customizing content for individual markets and languages. Adobe GenStudio solutions also help ensure that every piece of content created adheres to brand standards and preserves the look, tone and feel of the NHL experience.
The right experience, wherever fans engage: The league will leverage Adobe Experience Platform, which can provide a real-time view into customer needs and preferences. These insights can be activated through Adobe Journey Optimizer—the customer journey management solution—and allow the NHL to deliver the right fan experience, at just the right moment. With real-time customer insights, the League can also help make content produced in Adobe GenStudio tailored to individuals, across major channels such as app, web, email and in-arena. Whether it is a fan browsing stats online or experiencing a game in-person, they can receive relevant content that speaks to their tastes and preferences. This helps centralize personalization efforts as a League-wide initiative that keeps pace with consumer expectations, going beyond market-by-market experiments that are difficult to scale.
Fans could become creators: Looking ahead, Adobe Express—the quick and easy create-anything app—could give NHL fans new ways to convey their passion for the game. With the ability to use generative AI capabilities powered by Adobe Firefly for high-quality image generation, along with NHL-themed templates, fans could create compelling content designed to be easily shared across channels such as social media. Adobe Express could also allow each piece of content to be personalized based on individual creativity.
The partnership will enhance the fan experience across the NHL’s global footprint and its 32 Club markets, spanning some of the biggest moments including the Stanley Cup Playoffs, NHL Global Series, North American events and U.S. and international game broadcasts. As sports fandom moves beyond the arena—with fans looking to engage across social media, mobile app, live broadcasts and more—Adobe and the NHL are working together to ensure the League delivers an impactful experience across every moment. This will enable the League to bring the sport of hockey to a bigger audience and deepen the longstanding connection it has built with fans.

pages.title: Adobe Premiere finally brings powerful video editing to Android, and it's free - Ars Technica
pages.text:
Video editing has never been Android’s strong suit. While Apple has long offered iMovie for iPhone and iPad, Google has never had a comparable offering. Adobe is now stepping up to fill this feature gap with a proper version of Premiere. The app is now available in the Play Store for almost all Android devices, and it’s free (mostly).
Android’s version of Premiere doesn’t offer all the features you’d get in the desktop application, but it’s a big step up from the soon-to-be-retired Premiere Rush app. You can import as many video tracks as you want, trim them, split them, add effects, and export videos in up to 4K resolution. It can even extract audio from clips, reduce background noise, and add voiceovers. The app emphasizes the YouTube Short format, even defaulting your video outputs to portrait 16:9, but you can change that to something more traditional.
On a standard smartphone, the app splits the screen with the timeline at the bottom and preview up top. Adobe says that Premiere is optimized for multiple form factors. If you have a foldable phone, the UI adjusts to give you more breathing room, placing the timeline to the right of the video. That makes sense as the default, as Premiere wants you to make YouTube Shorts, but if you’re working with something wider, there’s a layout toggle that puts the widescreen video above the expanded timeline. The split is also adjustable if you want to make your video or timeline larger.
I tested Premiere by importing multiple high-bitrate 4K clips, and it didn’t choke. However, processing newly added video tracks can take a minute. Exporting is also not instant, but it’s faster than I expected on a Pixel, which isn’t exactly known for extreme performance. A three-minute 4K60 video in high-quality mode took about three minutes. The app is designed to work on any Android device with at least 5GB of RAM.
Credit:
Credit:
There are a good number of options in the editing interface—unless you’re a pro or enthusiast video editor, this app should be more than powerful enough. Adobe also says that Premiere (and the rest of its mobile app portfolio) is optimized for Googlebook laptops. If you need more, there’s always the full desktop version of Premiere. Of course, that won’t be an option on Googlebooks.
Premiere for Android is free, and you don’t even need a subscription or Creative Cloud account unless you care about generative AI tools. The new Premiere app has image-to-video and text-to-video, with options for Adobe’s “commercial safe” Firefly model as well as Google Veo, Google Omni, Luma Ray, and Kling models.
You can generate some clips for free in Premiere, which comes with 250 monthly AI credits. That’s enough for a few Veo Fast clips (80 credits each) or a single Firefly video. For $70 per year or $8 per month, you get 1,200 monthly AI credits in the Premiere mobile app. If that’s not your thing, you can just enjoy the free, vastly improved video editing experience on Android. Apple devices got this app last year, but “better late than never” has always been the Android app motto.
Ryan Whitwam is a senior technology reporter at Ars Technica, covering the ways Google, AI, and mobile technology continue to change the world. Over his 20-year career, he's written for Android Police, ExtremeTech, Wirecutter, NY Times, and more. He has reviewed more phones than most people will ever own. Unity Software Surges 5% as Traders Weigh Meta Platforms VR Glasses Support; Adobe Rises 3%, Intuit Adds 2%
Unity Software jumped after announcing day-one support for Meta's next-generation VR headset, but a timely product catalyst and a struggling business are not the same thing, and traders now face the harder question of which one matters more.
Published September 30, 2026, 2:12pm ET · 3 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
A dynamic representation of market growth, featuring a digital trading interface, a rising candlestick chart, and a powerful bull symbolizing a strong upward trend in stock performance. © Shutterstock
Unity Software (NYSE:U | U Price Prediction) stock rose 5% to $41.56 as traders weighed the company’s newly announced day-one support for Meta VR Glasses. The product news arrives as Unity works to reinforce its role in extended-reality development, though concerns around sales growth and billings still give investors reasons to remain selective.
The broader software group also moved higher. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (BATS:IGV) gained 1.5% to $106.81, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE ARCA:SPY) added 0.41% to $767.30.
Unity announced immediate engine support for Meta VR Glasses, Meta Platforms’ next-generation virtual-reality device that is expected to reach retail customers in spring 2027. Unity said developers can begin building and testing experiences now, providing more time to prepare titles for the device’s launch.
For existing Quest developers, Unity said projects built with OpenXR can carry forward with minimal changes. The company also highlighted support for eye and hand tracking, quad views rendering that can reduce GPU demands, and spatial-audio tools designed for more immersive experiences.
Unity’s early compatibility could make the engine more attractive to studios planning games, entertainment products, training software, and other immersive applications for Meta VR Glasses. The company said developers can test certain VR Glasses interactions within the Unity Editor before receiving physical hardware.
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) is central to the opportunity because Meta VR Glasses will sit within the same ecosystem as Meta’s existing Quest products. Unity said existing Quest apps can run on VR Glasses from day one, which could reduce development friction for studios already using Unity’s tools.
That compatibility matters because developers typically prefer to reuse assets, workflows, and code across multiple devices when possible. Unity’s product announcement emphasized a single codebase that can support multiple platforms, potentially helping studios reach additional players without rebuilding projects from scratch.
The opportunity, however, depends on adoption after Meta brings VR Glasses to market. Unity may need to demonstrate that developers are using the new tools, launching successful projects, and expanding their subscriptions or platform spending before the announcement becomes a meaningful financial catalyst.
Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) stock climbed 3% to $239.37, adding to the software-sector strength. Adobe remains closely associated with creative and document software, making Adobe stock a familiar way for investors to track demand for productivity tools and AI-enhanced workflows.
Intuit (NASDAQ:INTU) stock gained 2% to $273.21 as software names broadly advanced. Intuit operates consumer and business-focused financial software platforms, and Intuit stock can respond to expectations for customer growth, recurring revenue, and operating leverage.
The gains in Adobe stock and Intuit stock helped show that Unity’s move was not occurring in complete isolation. Still, Unity’s 5% rise outpaced both peers and the IGV ETF, suggesting that the Meta VR Glasses news gave traders a company-specific reason to focus on Unity.
Unity Stock: Growth Questions Remain Important
The positive product headline does not eliminate the concerns surrounding Unity’s underlying business performance. Recent commentary has pointed to stagnant sales, slower billings growth, and a stock that has remained under pressure despite the latest 5% advance.
Unity’s long-term case may depend on whether new platform support translates into broader Create-segment demand and more durable revenue growth. The company has a clear technical story around VR Glasses, yet investors will likely want evidence that product momentum is producing measurable business results.
For now, Unity stock has a timely catalyst, while Adobe stock and Intuit stock are participating in a broader software-sector rally. Investors should watch for signs that Unity’s VR Glasses support leads to new developer adoption, launch titles, and stronger financial metrics, while keeping position sizes modest given the company’s execution risks.

Adobe (ADBE) Ties Up New AI Fan Deal Reaching 200 Million Followers
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 1:10 AM PDT 2 min read
Adobe (NasdaqGS: ADBE) has entered a new partnership with the National Hockey League to deliver AI powered fan experiences worldwide.
The collaboration aims to serve more than 200 million NHL followers with personalized content and engagement tools across international markets.
Adobe is providing AI, creativity, and marketing products as core technology infrastructure for the league's global fan experience programs.
This NHL partnership with Adobe's AI platform sits within a wider pattern of moves that research has already highlighted for this business. Take a look at 1 warning sign we have identified for Adobe.

NasdaqGS:ADBE Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Sep 2026
Adobe operates as a global software group focused on creativity, digital documents, and marketing tools, which gives it a natural role supplying the AI infrastructure behind this kind of large-scale sports engagement. With a market value of about $89.9b, the business already works at the scale required to support major leagues and international fan bases.
4 things going right for Adobe that this headline doesn't cover.
How does this NHL deal fit Adobe's broader AI push?
The NHL agreement puts Adobe's CX Enterprise stack, GenStudio and Experience Platform in front of more than 200 million followers across 147 countries. That reach lines up with Adobe's wider focus on AI driven content workflows and marketing, similar to its Jet2 alliance in travel and its work around AI influenced holiday shopping.
What synergies could matter most for Adobe and the NHL?
NHL clubs get a shared toolkit for real time fan insight, personalized journeys and brand consistent content across 32 teams, while Adobe gets a single high profile setting to show how its products work as a complete customer experience system. The same tools that power hockey content can translate into templates for other large leagues and media owners.

The clearest early test is whether the NHL scales Adobe tools from pilots to league wide usage during the 2026 to 2027 season, measured through adoption across all 32 clubs and more personalized engagement in key events like the Stanley Cup Playoffs and NHL Global Series broadcasts.

ServiceNow Climbs 4% as Software Names Lead a Rebound; Intuit Jumps 4%, Adobe Rises 3%
Enterprise software names are surging ahead of the broader tech market, but one company in the group carries something the others do not, and it changes how you should read this rally.
Published October 1, 2026, 9:33am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
ServiceNow's modern headquarters, symbolizing the company's strong performance as its AI business crosses the $1 billion annual contract value mark, influencing its stock forecast. © Sundry Photography / iStock Editorial via Getty Images
Enterprise software is leading a rebound across technology stocks, and shares of ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW | NOW Price Prediction) sit at the front of the group. ServiceNow stock is up 4% to $139.73, moving in step with the closest names in application software. Gains are spread across several major application vendors at once, a sign of broad sector participation.
Also, shares of Intuit (NASDAQ:INTU) are up 4% to $285.50, matching the gain in ServiceNow stock. Meanwhile, Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) shares are climbing 3% to $246.49, a slightly smaller gain pointed the same way. Workday (NASDAQ:WDAY) rounds out the enterprise software cluster, adding another large application vendor exposed to the same artificial intelligence (AI) debate.
Notably, the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (CBOE:IGV) is up 1% to $107.95. The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 0.5% to $743.20, a smaller advance for large-cap technology. Software’s lead over that broader benchmark marks this as a group bid concentrated in application vendors.
ServiceNow stock’s rally tracks a broad bid across enterprise software. The software sector fund is beating large-cap technology, and the two closest peers, Intuit and Adobe, are moving the same direction by similar amounts. That combination points to sector repair across the group, and ServiceNow stock is benefiting as money flows back into application software, since broad buying of that kind tends to lift the strongest operators and the weakest ones alike.
Workday belongs to the enterprise software cluster and faces the same questions about how AI changes application spending. Alongside ServiceNow, Intuit, and Adobe, Workday gives the group coverage of workflow, financial, creative, and human resources software, so the rebound reaches well beyond one product category. That breadth makes the enterprise cluster a cleaner read on sector sentiment than any single stock.
Disclosed AI Revenue Separates ServiceNow
Inside the group, ServiceNow carries a distinguishing fact: its AI products are already producing disclosed revenue. In the most recently reported quarter, ServiceNow stated that annual contract value from its AI products exceeded $1 billion. That figure speaks to the first argument around the company, which is whether AI products convert into reported sales.
ServiceNow also reported a renewal rate of 98% in that quarter, a sign the subscription base is holding while the market debates whether generative AI replaces software-as-a-service applications. Together, the two disclosures give ServiceNow stock stronger fundamental basis than a sector bounce supplies on its own.
For ServiceNow, a clear signal is whether the IGV fund keeps its lead over the broader technology benchmark, and traders can watch for whether that spread holds because it defines the rally lifting ServiceNow, Intuit, and Adobe shares. Any closing of that gap would suggest the software bid is fading into a more dull technology tone.
Traders should watch Intuit and Adobe shares. If they stop moving in step with ServiceNow stock, that split would hurt the sector-repair reading. A strong next quarterly update from ServiceNow could confirm that AI contract value keeps converting into reported revenue.
ServiceNow pairs disclosed AI traction with a 98% renewal rate, which reinforces the case for upside, while the displacement debate supports caution. Those holding the stock should size their positions carefully given that a single rally for software leaves that debate unresolved.

Adobe’s Rollercoaster Ride Continues: Who’s Buying?
Mon, September 28, 2026 at 4:26 AM PDT 5 min read
Adobe trades at 9x forward earnings with a PEG of 0.58 despite AI-first ARR topping $650 million and growing over 150%.
Adobe fell 33% over the past year while the S&P 500 gained 17%, yet analysts' average price target of $278 implies 18% upside.
A Buy upgrade requires proof that 100 million freemium users are converting to paid subscribers under new CEO Chakravarthy.
Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)
Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) is a Hold at $235.47. Shares of the creative software leader trade as if the business were in decline, yet the company keeps raising its guidance.
Adobe makes Photoshop, Premiere, Acrobat and a customer experience suite that serves over 20,000 global enterprises. Third-quarter revenue rose 12.9% to $6.76 billion. Non-GAAP EPS of $6.13 was its 5th consecutive EPS beat. The stock still fell 32.72% year to date. Investors worry about generative AI rivals, a CEO transition to Anil Chakravarthy and the exit of the company's former CFO.
Nine Times Forward Earnings for a Double-Digit Grower
Bulls see a mispricing. Adobe trades at 9x forward earnings with a PEG ratio of 0.582. Management raised its full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance from an initial $23.30 to $23.50 to $24.45 to $24.50. AI-first ARR now tops $650 million and is growing more than 150%, which shows that customers pay for Firefly and agentic tools.
Capital returns support the case. Free cash flow rose 14.68% to $2.44 billion, and Adobe retired ~9.5M shares for $2.232B with approximately $24.55 billion of authorization remaining. On the insider side, Director David Ricks purchased 10,000 shares at $194.513 on the open market.
AI Rivals and Leadership Churn Test Adobe's Moat
Bears point to profits lagging sales. Net income grew just 3.1% in the quarter, while RPO growth slowed to 8%. Management put Creative Cloud price increases on hold to guide users into freemium, and it said that the shift pressures net new ARR.

Adobe's execution rules out a Sell, and the unclear AI outlook rules out a Buy. The stock sits below its 50-day average of $257.41 and its 200-day average of $263.2, so momentum has not turned. At $235.47, Adobe is a Hold.
The valuation already prices in a lot of bad news, but buying the stock needs a reason for it to rebound. The first trigger for a Buy is fourth-quarter results that meet guidance of $6.80B to $6.85B in revenue with a margin near 44.0%, together with a increase in RPO growth. The second is proof that freemium users, now over 100 million on the creative side alone, are turning into paying subscribers.
A Sell case would build if ARR growth misses the 10.2% target or if analysts cut fiscal 2027 estimates, which currently average 27.6226. Because the stock has a beta of 1.417, it can swing sharply in either direction.

Adobe's stock has collapsed while its revenue keeps hitting records, and Wall Street is stuck in a holding pattern. A specific combination of catalysts could change that calculus dramatically before 2027 is over.
Published September 30, 2026, 8:30am ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
The Adobe logo prominently displayed on a brick building, symbolizing the company's solid foundation and its successful decade-long transformation into a subscription powerhouse. © David Tran / iStock Editorial via Getty Images
Adobe’s problem is perception. Investors worry that AI-native tools will chip away at Photoshop, Premiere and Acrobat. The business keeps growing anyway.
In fiscal Q3, Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE | ADBE Price Prediction) posted record revenue of $6.76 billion, up 12.89% year over year. AI-first ARR passed $650 million and grew more than 150%.
“We’re just beginning to capitalize on the massive AI opportunity across creativity, productivity, and customer experiences,” said outgoing CEO Shantanu Narayen.
The stock has gone the other way. Shares are down 34.34% year-to-date at $229.82 and 63.09% over five years. So what would it take for Adobe to hit $300 in 2027?
Wall Street Sees 21% Upside as Estimates Creep Higher
Analysts’ average price target of $278.15 implies about 21% upside. Sentiment is lukewarm, with 23 Hold ratings. The numbers are stronger than the mood. Consensus calls for EPS of $24.4735 in FY2026, rising to $27.6226 in FY2027. That works out to roughly 13% EPS growth on about 9% revenue growth. The FY2027 estimate has also edged up from $27.5501 90 days ago.
Adobe also keeps beating expectations. Q3 non-GAAP EPS came in at $6.13, against a consensus of $6.0866. That was the fifth consecutive beat, so actual results could top today’s forecasts.
Here’s What It Takes for Adobe to Reach $300
At $229.82, Adobe trades at about 8x FY2027 earnings estimates. At $300, that multiple would be about 11x. That’s still well below the S&P 500’s forward multiple of roughly 21x to 23x, and Adobe guides for a Q4 non-GAAP operating margin of about 44%.
What Could Push Adobe to $300?
AI monetization: Firefly ending ARR grew 40% quarter over quarter. Management also put pricing increases on hold to keep adding users, so that option is still available for 2027.
A huge user base: Monthly active users passed one billion. Creative freemium users crossed 100 million, growing greater than 70%.
Buybacks: Adobe bought back about 9.5 million shares in Q3, and $24.55 billion remains under its current authorization.
New leadership: Anil Chakravarthy becomes CEO on December 1st. “I see immense opportunity for Adobe to be the leader in agentic software for creativity, productivity, and customer experience,” he said.
Near-term events: Adobe MAX and the Topaz Labs deal, set to close in Q4, both come ahead of a seasonally strong enterprise quarter.
The risks: a weak market, a rough CEO transition or faster-moving AI rivals would make $300 harder to reach.
Getting to $300 requires a gain of about 31%. Adobe has done better than that in 10 calendar years since 2000. Shares rose 77% in 2023 and 70% in 2017.
The most useful comparison may be 2009, when the stock rallied 73% from a low starting point. With a market cap of $91.35 billion, Adobe is small enough that a move that size is realistic.
$300 Is a Stretch, but Adobe Has the Tools to Get There
Reaching $300 would take a 31% gain, more than the 21% Wall Street already guides for.
Several things support it: growing AI revenue, a billion users, a string of earnings beats and one of the lowest valuations among large software companies. If the new CEO settles in smoothly and the market cooperates, shares could return to 11x earnings. Returns this large shouldn’t be expected every year, but this is how Adobe could deliver outsized gains in 2027.

pages.title: Adobe Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
pages.text:
Skip to navigation Skip to main content Skip to right column
Interested in Adobe Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.
Strong Q3 performance: Adobe reported revenue of $6.76 billion, up 13% year over year, with non-GAAP EPS rising 15% to $6.13. Annual recurring revenue reached $27.5 billion, while AI-first ending ARR exceeded $650 million, growing more than 150%.
Leadership transition: Anil Chakravarthy will become Adobe's president and CEO on Dec. 1, while current CEO Shantanu Narayen will move to executive chair. Chakravarthy plans to focus on "agentic software" across Adobe's creative, productivity and customer-experience businesses.
Raised fiscal 2026 outlook: Adobe increased its full-year revenue forecast to $26.576 billion-$26.626 billion and non-GAAP EPS guidance to $24.45-$24.50, supported by adoption of Firefly, Acrobat AI and enterprise AI products.
The SaaSpocalypse Trade Is Cracking, and These 5 Stocks Are Leading Higher
Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue of $6.76 billion, up 13% year over year as reported and 12% in constant currency, while also announcing a leadership transition that will take effect Dec. 1.
Chair and CEO Shantanu Narayen said GAAP earnings per share rose 11% from a year earlier to $4.62, while non-GAAP EPS increased 15% to $6.13. The company ended the quarter with $27.5 billion in annual recurring revenue, up 11.2% year over year, and generated a quarterly record of $2.52 billion in operating cash flow.
→ IBM and Lockheed Martin Turn a Swiss Defense Deal Into a Quantum Computing Bet
Buy the Dip or Run: 3 Software Stocks Down 50% Face Their Moment of Truth
Narayen said Adobe's AI-first ending ARR exceeded $650 million and grew more than 150% year over year. The company said it has more than 1 billion monthly active users across its businesses, including more than 100 million creative freemium users, which grew more than 70% year over year.
Adobe said Anil Chakravarthy, currently president of customer experience and orchestration, will become the company's next president, chief executive officer and a member of its board effective Dec. 1. Narayen, who has spent 29 years at Adobe, will serve as executive chair and said he will work with Chakravarthy to support the transition.
→ Kroger's Textbook Entry for Buy-and-Hold Investors
Adobe Stock Just Got Cheaper—Is Wall Street Missing the Story?
"Anil is the right person to chart Adobe's growth in this agentic era," Narayen said, citing Chakravarthy's experience building products across Adobe's businesses.
Chakravarthy said he sees an opportunity for Adobe to lead in "agentic software" across creativity, productivity and customer experience. He said customers are seeking software that supports conversational and traditional interfaces, offers access to various AI models, incorporates enterprise context and data, and delivers predictable results.
→ Could Snowflake's Big Quarter Be a Sign of More to Come?
In response to analyst questions, Chakravarthy said his experience leading Adobe's enterprise field operations since 2020 has given him exposure to all of the company's product categories and customer segments, from individuals and small businesses to more than 20,000 enterprise customers.
Document and Creative Businesses Post Subscription Growth
Subscription revenue from Adobe's business professionals and consumers segment was $1.91 billion, up 16% as reported and 15% in constant currency. The company said Acrobat plus Express monthly active users surpassed 900 million, rising more than 25% year over year, while Acrobat AI Assistant monthly active users doubled sequentially.
Chakravarthy highlighted new Acrobat capabilities powered by the Adobe Productivity Agent. According to the company, the offerings can turn documents into interactive reports, summary slides and audio formats, while new knowledge-base and analysis functions allow teams to query large document collections. Adobe also said it expanded Acrobat access across platforms including ChatGPT, Chrome, Microsoft Edge and WhatsApp.
Creative and marketing professional subscription revenue totaled $4.65 billion, up 13% as reported and 12% in constant currency. Adobe said Firefly ending ARR from its application and credit packs grew 40% sequentially, supported by accelerating credit consumption across Creative Cloud and Firefly.
Narayen told analysts that video generation has been a particular driver of Firefly activity. He also said AI credit consumption has been robust in Adobe's core Creative Cloud desktop applications, reflecting broader integration of AI into product usage.
Adobe said it expanded its Creative Agent into Photoshop and Premiere and added native generation of music, speech and sound effects to Firefly. The company also announced an agreement to acquire Topaz Labs, whose AI enhancement technology is expected to be integrated into Creative Cloud, Firefly and Adobe's enterprise creative offerings. Adobe expects the transaction to close in the fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions.
Adobe said its customer experience strategy centers on Adobe Experience Platform and customer-engagement applications, GenStudio for content supply chains, and Experience Manager and agentic web applications for brand visibility.
The company introduced Adobe Brand Visibility, which combines Semrush AI visibility intelligence with Adobe's content-optimization capabilities. Adobe said the product uses a database of nearly 300 million real-world AI search prompts to help customers understand how their brands appear across platforms including ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot and Perplexity AI.
Adobe said the number of paid customers for brand-visibility solutions doubled sequentially. It also reported more than 1,700 customers and early adopters of CX Enterprise Coworker, an AI agent that coordinates marketing and customer-engagement workflows across analytics, content creation and journey orchestration.
Ending ARR for Adobe Experience Manager and agentic web applications, Adobe GenStudio, and Adobe Experience Platform and applications each increased more than 20% year over year, according to the company.
For the fourth quarter, Adobe forecast total revenue of $6.8 billion to $6.85 billion, including business professionals and consumer subscription revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and creative and marketing professional subscription revenue of $4.665 billion to $4.695 billion. The company projected GAAP EPS of $4.65 to $4.70 and non-GAAP EPS of $6.30 to $6.35.
Adobe raised its full-year fiscal 2026 outlook, targeting:
Total revenue of $26.576 billion to $26.626 billion.
Business professionals and consumer subscription revenue of $7.47 billion to $7.49 billion.
Creative and marketing professional subscription revenue of $18.242 billion to $18.272 billion.
GAAP EPS of $18.12 to $18.17.
Non-GAAP EPS of $24.45 to $24.50.
Interim CFO Steve Day said the company's updated fourth-quarter outlook reflected a roughly $50 million increase at the midpoint from its prior guidance, although foreign exchange creates a slight headwind. He said Adobe expects the fourth quarter to remain seasonally strong, particularly for enterprise activity.
Adobe repurchased approximately 9.5 million shares during the quarter and ended the period with $5.64 billion in cash and short-term investments. The company said it had approximately $24.55 billion remaining under its April 2026 share-repurchase authorization.
Adobe Inc (NASDAQ:ADBE) develops software and services used for digital content creation, document management and digital experiences. The company serves creative professionals, marketers, enterprises, educators and consumers worldwide through subscription-based and cloud-enabled products.
Adobe's Creative Cloud portfolio includes applications such as Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere Pro and After Effects, along with related tools for photography, graphic design, video production and web development.

Adobe’s Rollercoaster Ride Continues: Who’s Buying?
Adobe keeps beating earnings estimates while its stock collapses, leaving investors to wonder whether Wall Street is pricing in a threat that may never materialize or a disruption that already has.
Published September 28, 2026, 7:26am ET · 3 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Adobe is a multinational software company best known for its Photoshop and Acrobat. © Adobe logo (CC by 2.0) by midiman
Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE | ADBE Price Prediction) is a Hold at $235.47. Shares of the creative software leader trade as if the business were in decline, yet the company keeps raising its guidance.
Adobe makes Photoshop, Premiere, Acrobat and a customer experience suite that serves over 20,000 global enterprises. Third-quarter revenue rose 12.9% to $6.76 billion. Non-GAAP EPS of $6.13 was its 5th consecutive EPS beat. The stock still fell 32.72% year to date. Investors worry about generative AI rivals, a CEO transition to Anil Chakravarthy and the exit of the company’s former CFO.
Nine Times Forward Earnings for a Double-Digit Grower
Bulls see a mispricing. Adobe trades at 9x forward earnings with a PEG ratio of 0.582. Management raised its full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance from an initial $23.30 to $23.50 to $24.45 to $24.50. AI-first ARR now tops $650 million and is growing more than 150%, which shows that customers pay for Firefly and agentic tools.
Capital returns support the case. Free cash flow rose 14.68% to $2.44 billion, and Adobe retired ~9.5M shares for $2.232B with approximately $24.55 billion of authorization remaining. On the insider side, Director David Ricks purchased 10,000 shares at $194.513 on the open market.
AI Rivals and Leadership Churn Test Adobe’s Moat
Bears point to profits lagging sales. Net income grew just 3.1% in the quarter, while RPO growth slowed to 8%. Management put Creative Cloud price increases on hold to guide users into freemium, and it said that the shift pressures net new ARR.
Competition is getting louder. One widely discussed Reddit post read: “OpenAI releases ChatGPT Images 2.5. I expect Adobe stocks to nosedive once mass media gets a hold of this.” Add a $70M goodwill impairment in Publishing and Advertising, and the market views a business in transition.
A New CEO’s First Moves Decide the Next Leg
Adobe’s execution rules out a Sell, and the unclear AI outlook rules out a Buy. The stock sits below its 50-day average of $257.41 and its 200-day average of $263.2, so momentum has not turned. The next few months bring Adobe MAX, Chakravarthy’s first strategy statements as CEO, the close of the Topaz Labs deal and a seasonally strong fourth quarter.
Across 40 analysts, the average price target is $278.15, which implies about 18.1% upside. Price targets reflect analysts’ views and often miss. The ratings break down as follows:
The stock trades at 13x trailing earnings, inside a 52-week range of $190.12 to $363.7. Over the past year, Adobe fell 33.51% while the S&P 500 rose 17.22%. Over the past month, the stock dropped 13.9% against a 0.69% rose for the index.
At $235.47, Adobe is a Hold.
The valuation already prices in a lot of bad news, but buying the stock needs a reason for it to rebound. The first trigger for a Buy is fourth-quarter results that meet guidance of $6.80B to $6.85B in revenue with a margin near 44.0%, together with a increase in RPO growth. The second is proof that freemium users, now over 100 million on the creative side alone, are turning into paying subscribers.
A Sell case would build if ARR growth misses the 10.2% target or if analysts cut fiscal 2027 estimates, which currently average 27.6226. Because the stock has a beta of 1.417, it can swing sharply in either direction.
Waiting costs little. The stock pays no dividend, and the new CEO’s first full quarter will show whether Adobe’s AI spending leads to profit growth. At this price, patience lets investors see the new CEO’s results before taking a position.

Where Could Adobe's Next Growth Come From?
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 12:03 PM PDT 4 min read
Adobe's revenue grew 12% over the last year, slower than most of its big software peers. The share price appears to assume that its growth is fading. Over the last year, the stock fell 35%, while the S&P 500 returned 17.7%. Adobe (ADBE) trades at 12.5 times its earnings, against 22.1 for the index. Management pointed to a small, fast-growing line on its fiscal Q3 2026 call. Is that going to be enough? Where could Adobe's next real growth come from?
Adobe's Next Growth Could Come From Its AI Products
The small line is Adobe's (ADBE) AI-first products. They are growing far faster than the rest of the company. Management said their ending annual recurring revenue, or ARR, exceeded $650 million in fiscal Q3 2026. ARR is the yearly value of the subscriptions customers hold at the end of a quarter. That figure grew more than 150% from a year earlier, against 11.2% for Adobe's total ARR.
Adobe's Firefly products are growing quickly. Ending ARR from the Firefly app and Firefly credit packs grew 40% from the previous quarter. Customers are also using more AI. Management said AI credit use accelerated from the previous quarter, across Creative Cloud and the Firefly app. Adobe's AI products are growing fast, but they start from a small base.
How Big Are Adobe's AI Products So Far?
Of every $100 of Adobe's recurring revenue, about $2.40 comes from AI-first products. Total ending ARR was $27.5 billion in fiscal Q3 2026. At that scale, AI-first products are still an incremental part of Adobe.
Adobe as a whole is still growing, and a little faster than before. Revenue rose 12.0% over the last twelve months, up from 10.7% in the twelve months before that. The price appears to assume that this pace will not last. Adobe's earnings multiple is in the bottom tenth of its own 10-year range.
Say that the fast-growing line keeps growing while Adobe as a whole holds its pace. Then the assumption of fading growth would be harder to square with the numbers.
What Would Show Adobe's Free-User Push Is Paying Off?
Adobe chose to drive new user adoption rather than focus on pricing actions. The free-user push has a cost today. Net new ARR is the recurring revenue added during a period. A question on the fiscal Q3 2026 call put net new ARR down 36% to 37% from a year earlier.
Management answered that Adobe is balancing new customers against ARR growth, sending new users through its free tier first. That free tier is large. Monthly active users of Adobe's free creative tools passed 100 million, up more than 70% from a year earlier.
Management said the slower RPO growth reflects its focus on adding new users through its free tier. So the first sign of a payoff would be faster growth from a year earlier in Adobe's contracted revenue.
Contracted revenue shows up in remaining performance obligations, or RPO. RPO is revenue customers have signed for that Adobe has not yet booked. RPO grew 8% from a year earlier. A question on the same call noted this was RPO's first single-digit growth since early fiscal 2023. Management said RPO steps up in the fourth quarter and then stays fairly flat for three quarters. So a fourth-quarter step-up on its own is the normal pattern, not proof. Growth from a year earlier is what matters.
Adobe MAX, the company's creativity conference, is set for November in Miami Beach. Management said major Firefly and Creative Cloud releases are planned in the run-up to it.
Adobe's AI products are its clearest new source of growth, but they are still a small part of the business. The fiscal Q4 2026 report will show whether RPO growth rises from the 8% it posted in fiscal Q3 2026. If it stays in single digits, the free-user push has not yet paid off.

Shares of Adobe (ADBE -1.49%) have had a tough 2026. The stock ended last year at about $350 and trades near $240 as I write, down about 31%.
The software company has kept buying its own shares on the way down. In April, its board approved a new $25 billion stock buyback authorization, meant partly to "reduce share count over time." It runs through April 30, 2030.
And as Adobe's fiscal third quarter of 2026 ended Aug. 28, $24.55 billion of it was still unused.
Compared with Adobe's market value, the amount is large. With about 389.2 million shares outstanding in mid-September, Adobe is worth about $93 billion at today's stock price. The remaining authorization could buy back about 26% of it -- about 102 million shares.
Sure, an authorization isn't a promise. Adobe has around three and a half years to use it, and nothing forces the company to spend it all. But I think the company's pace this year shows it plans to put plenty of it to work.
Image source: Getty Images.
In the fiscal year's first three quarters, Adobe's buybacks averaged around $2.3 billion a quarter. That came to $6.82 billion, for 26.1 million shares, all bought on the open market.
And as the stock dropped, the same money bought more shares. The 9.5 million shares Adobe repurchased in fiscal Q3 cost an average of around $235 each, versus about $261 over all three quarters.
Notably, the company paid for it with cash from its operations. Adobe generated $7.65 billion of cash from operations during the same stretch, up around 11% year over year, and buybacks used close to 90% of it. Its balance sheet had $5.64 billion of cash and short-term investments at quarter-end, versus around $6.4 billion of debt.
This pace leaves room to spare. Spreading the unspent $24.55 billion evenly through April 2030 comes out to around $7 billion a year, about what Adobe spent in just those three quarters. If the company keeps buying at its recent rate instead, it could use up the authorization sometime in 2029.

At roughly $240, Adobe shares cost about 13 times earnings. True, a buyback can't fix slowing growth. You can open a PDF, select AI Assistant, and type a question or choose a suggested one. Adobe’s documentation describes answers with source citations and follow-up suggestions.
For researchers, useful questions might include:
What research question does this paper address?
How did the authors select their participants?
Which limitations do they acknowledge?
Where do they explain this finding?
I would begin with a specific question tied to the document. Asking where the authors discuss a limitation is more manageable than requesting a judgement about whether the entire study is trustworthy.

SAN JOSE and NEW YORK -- Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE) — the global technology leader that unleashes creativity, productivity and customer experiences through innovative tools and platforms — and the National Hockey League (NHL) have announced a partnership to transform fan experiences with AI. As the NHL gets ready to drop the puck on the 2026-27 regular season, Adobe becomes an Official Creative, Marketing and AI Partner of the NHL. Adobe will provide AI technology to help power how the NHL creates and personalizes fan experiences across every touchpoint, as the League looks to expand its footprint globally (with over 200 million fans across 147 countries) and deepen engagement with its audiences. The partnership could also provide fans new creativity tools to express their passion for the sport and its Players.
“The NHL's greatest strength has always been the passion our fans bring to the game,” said David Lehanski, NHL Executive Vice President of Innovation and Growth Strategy. “As the ways people follow sports continue to evolve, our focus is on creating experiences that feel as dynamic and compelling as the game itself.
